title: Abdominal pain or gastrointestinal bleeding
summary: Abdominal pain, vomiting blood or blood in the stool. Localized pain and possible bleeding are shown as findings. A digestive cause is only considered with sufficient evidence. Informational support only: not a diagnosis or a treatment decision. No clinical personnel on board: the steps are first aid and monitoring; treatment depends on mission procedures.

immediate.text: Sudden, severe abdominal pain, vomiting blood or black stools: emergency.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Call for emergency help now using the mission's means (ship alarm, crew, mission control if the link is up). Do not wait to see if it gets better.
Do not take any medication on your own.

prompt_review.text: Persistent, focal or worsening abdominal pain, or blood in the stool: monitor closely.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Take sips of water or other clear fluids and avoid solid food for the first few hours.
Do not take any medication on your own.
If the pain becomes sudden and sharp, you vomit blood, your stools are black or bloody, your abdomen is rigid or you have trouble breathing, treat it as an emergency.

review.text: Abdominal pain: take care of yourself and monitor. If it becomes sudden and severe or bleeding appears, it is an emergency.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

candidates.label: Digestive cause
candidates.minimum_evidence: Abdominal pain with nausea, vomiting or diarrhea.
